slides.title: Urinary Elimination
text: Methods: midstream collection or catheter collection
Results may indicate a change in medication
How do we perform  a 24-hour creatinine clearance?

slides.title: Urine Specific Gravity
text: Measurement of the concentration of particles (waste & electrolytes in the urine)
A high SG indicates concentrated urine
A low SG indicates diluted urine

slides.title: Urinary Elimination Hygiene
text: Assist with voiding: running water, hands in water, standing etc.

slides.title: Urinary Tract Infection
text: Most common of the nosocomial infection's d/t catheters, wiping back to front
S/S: dysuria, frequency, urgency, fever, chills, N/V, malaise, hematuria, cloudy urine, flank pain and tenderness
Treatment: antibiotics, fluids, acid-ash foods (meat, eggs, poultry, cereals, bread, cranberry juice)
What do we educate about UTI prevention?

slides.title: Urinary EliminationUrinary Incontinence
text: Identified as functional, overflow, reflex, stress or urge incontinence
Condition that can be socially isolating and underreported to physicians
S/S: urgency, dysuria, frequency, polyuria, oliguria, anuria, nocturia, hematuria, dribbling, residual urine

slides.title: Urinary Elimination Restorative care
text: Used for stress incontinence, overactive bladder
Regular toileting schedule, relax to aid complete emptying, methods to initiate voiding, diuretic administration, minimize caffeine
Spinal cord injuries, neurogenic bladder, degenerative muscle disease
How often should Kegel exercises be performed?

slides.title: Urinary EliminationTypes of Catheterization
text: Prevention of urinary obstruction from clots
Severe urinary retention with recurrent UTIs
Skin rashes, ulcers, or wounds irritated by contact w/ urine
Important to document the first voiding after catheter removed

slides.title: Urinary EliminationTypes of Catheterization
text: Assessment of residual urine after urination
Long term management w/ spinal cord, neuro muscular degeneration or incompetent bladders

slides.title: Factors Influencing Bowel Elimination
text: Diet: bulk- high fiber, fluid intake(2400-3000ml)
Drugs: Narcotics, sedatives cathartics, antidiarrheal, antibiotics, ASA, iron
What are some foods high in fiber?

slides.title: Bowel EliminationAssessment
text: 1.  Usual pattern, frequency, description of stool

slides.title: Bowel EliminationBowel Sounds
text: Audible passage of air and fluid created by peristalsis
It normally takes 5 to 20 minutes to hear
Hyperactive-Increased GI motility, inflammation of bowel, anxiety, diarrhea, bleeding, partial bowel obstruction( high-pitched and tinkling or rushes followed by silence)
Hypoactive-- peritonitis, paralytic ileus, or no obvious cause.

slides.title: Bowel EliminationFecal Impaction
text: Mass or collection of hardened feces in folds of rectum
Passage of liquid fecal seepage and no normal stool

slides.title: Bowel EliminationLaxatives and Cathartics
text: High fiber, absorbs H20, increases bulk
Obstruction if not given with 240ml H2O
Contraindicated in clients with fluid restrictions
Stool Softener-allows water and fat to penetrate stool
Of little value for treatment of chronic constipation

slides.title: Saline Magnesium Hydroxide (Milk of Magnesia) MOM
text: Saline Magnesium Hydroxide (Milk of Magnesia) MOM
Contain salt preparation not absorbed by intestines. Osmotic effect increased pressure in bowel to act as stimulant.
Acute emptying of intestine- Diagnostics tests, constipation
Not for long-term management of constipation. Contraindicated in clients with kidney dysfunction
Not for long-term use or pregnancy
Chronic use may cause fluid and electrolyte imbalance
Coat fecal contents, easy passage of stool. Reduces water absorption
Decrease absorption of fat soluble vitamins.  Can cause pneumonia if aspirated

slides.title: Bowel EliminationEnemas
text: Prevents escape of feces during surgery
Prepare intestines for certain diagnostic tests
Removes feces in instances of constipation or impaction
Introduces oil or medication into the rectum and sigmoid colon

slides.title: Hypertonic (Fleet phosphate)
text: Can be delegated to a CNA…but only this one!!

slides.title: Isotonic (physiologic saline)
text: 5mL soap to 1000mL of water, 110F, 18 inches above rectum

slides.title: Bowel EliminationEnema Procedure
text: Turn client to left lateral side(preferred) or any position except sitting
Hold bag 18” above level of rectum
Allow solution to run in slowly by gravity
If cramping occurs, clamp the tubing and wait until cramping stops. Then continue
If client becomes pale, diaphoretic, c/o nausea or vomiting.

slides.title: Bowel EliminationEnemas
text: Tap Water: Caution in children or adults with kidney or cardiac problems, may increase blood volume.
Water intoxication:  weakness, sweating, pallor, vomiting, cough or dizziness
Saline: Hx. of heart failure and abnormal Na. Retention may cause electrolyte imbalance
Soap Suds:  Too much or too strong soap can cause colon membrane damage.
Digital removal of stool: avoid vagal stimulation (pallor, diaphoresis, low HR)

slides.title: Bowel EliminationRectal Tube
text: To facilitate the expulsion of flatus.
Assess abdominal distention before and after and record

slides.title: Bowel EliminationRectal Suppository
text: Insert beyond internal sphincter, along side of intestine

slides.title: Bowel EliminationDiarrhea
text: May or may not have cramping

slides.title: Bowel EliminationDiarrhea
text: Monitor for fluid and electrolyte imbalance

slides.title: Bowel EliminationDiarrhea
text: Monitor for S&S of Atropine overdose: flushing, dry mouth, tachycardia, urinary retention, blurred vision

slides.title: Bowel EliminationColostomy or Ileostomy
text: A surgical creation of an opening (stoma) into the colon
Consistency of the drainage is related to the placement of the ostomy

slides.title: Bowel EliminationStoma
text: Opening created in the abdomen by the ostomy
Generally red in color and moist
Treat any irritation or skin breakdown immediately
Does a person feel a stoma?

slides.title: Assess peri stomal skin for irritation each time appliance changed
text: Assess peri stomal skin for irritation each time appliance changed
Keep skin clean by washing off any excretion and  pat drying thoroughly
Protect skin, collect stool, and control odor w/ an ostomy appliance
- Change product weekly - twice weekly; more prn
When should a client empty their ostomy pouch?

slides.title: Bowel EliminationStoma
text: Allows stoma expansion, decreases contact w/ stool/skin
Hold appliance in place for 30 seconds

slides.title: Apply a skin barrier (wafer, paste or powder) is used to protect the skin from fecal drainage.
text: Apply a skin barrier (wafer, paste or powder) is used to protect the skin from fecal drainage.
Nystatin powder can be ordered for irritation and yeast infection
Foods that cause excessive odor and gas are avoided

slides.title: Bowel EliminationIrrigation
text: Allow solution to run through tubing, catheter and cone(remove air in tube)
Lubricate and gently insert cone into stoma
Hold cone  in place- cone prevents fluid return
Begin flow, adjust flow by raising or lowering container about 18” above stoma
Allow water to enter slowly, 10 min.  Clamp for cramping.
Hold shield in place for 10 sec.

slides.title: Then dry the bottom of the sleeve and clamp.
text: Then dry the bottom of the sleeve and clamp.
Leave in place for 30-40 min., while client gets up and moves around
Cleanse area with mild soap and water, pat dry
Replace the colostomy dressing or pouch
Record the amount and appearance of stool or drainage in pouch, size of stoma, color of stool
Irrigation is only for colostomies not ileostomies.

slides.title: Mobility and ImmobilityBody Mechanics
text: Efficient, coordinated, and safe use of the body to move objects and carry out the activities of daily living

slides.title: Mobility and ImmobilityBody Mechanics
text: Bend Knees not back to lower center of gravity
Adjust working level to waist and keep body close to area
Carrying a tray near you body
Bending at knees to crank bed or empty catheter bag
Using a draw sheet to lift client up in bed or a Hoyer lift
Raising bed to waist level when providing client care measures
HOB down when moving client up in bed

slides.title: Mobility and ImmobilityRange of motion
text: client moves each joint through complete ROM
another person moves each joint through complete ROM
If spasticity occurs, stop movement temporarily
- Cont. applying firm, gentle pressure till relaxation occurs

slides.title: Mobility and ImmobilityTransfer
text: Make sure all wheels are locked
Get client OOB on the strong- unaffected side
Do a gradual transfer checking for dizziness etc.
Explain all procedures and support appropriately

slides.title: Assistance Devices
text: How do we teach the client use these devices?

slides.title: Sleep and Rest
text: Recurrent state of inactivity, with an altered state of consciousness that occurs for sustained periods
Time it takes to fall asleep
Number of times awakes at night

slides.title: Sleep and Rest
text: Dark circles, puffy, red, burning eyes

slides.title: Sleep and RestDisorders
text: Lack of airflow through the nose and mouth for periods of 10 seconds or longer during sleep
Obstructive is most common type – snoring & snorting
Arouses person from deep sleep to Stage II, thus person doesn’t get needed rest and has excessive daytime sleepiness
Chronic difficulty falling asleep, frequent awakenings, short sleep, insufficient quantity and quality of sleep

slides.title: Follow normal routine
text: Do not wake client up for prn sleep medications
PRN sleep meds should not be administered routinely--give when other measures fail
A drug that induces sleep.  Given at night

slides.title: Temazepam(Restoril)
text: Smaller doses are needed for the elderly
Do not suppress REM sleep to the extent of barbiturates

slides.title: Nutrition
text: Addition of solid food between 4 and 6 months
By age 1, infants can be completely fed on table food, and milk intake is about 20 ounces per day
Can eat most foods and adjust to 3 meals each day
By age 3, able to bite and chew adult table food
Need for adequate iron, calcium, and vitamins C and A are common deficiencies

slides.title: School-aged
text: Require a balanced diet including 2400 Kcal/day
Eat three meals a day and one or two nutritious snacks
Need a protein-rich food at breakfast to sustain the prolonged physical and mental effort required at school
Very active and often require snacks between meals
Cheese, fruits, yogurt, raw vegetables, and milk are good choices

slides.title: Adolescent
text: Increased need for nutrient and calories during growth spurts
Healthy snacks and limits on junk foods
Anorexia nervosa and bulimia may occur
Continue to eat a healthy diet, with special attention to protein, calcium, and limiting cholesterol and caloric intake
Two or three liters of fluid daily
Postmenopausal women need to ingest sufficient calcium and vitamin D to reduce osteoporosis

slides.title: Require the same basic nutrition as the younger  adult
text: Require the same basic nutrition as the younger  adult
Fewer calories are needed by elders because of the lower metabolic rate and the decrease in physical activity
Some may need more carbohydrates for fiber and bulk, but most nutrient requirements remain relatively unchanged
Physical changes as tooth loss and impaired sense of taste and smell may affect eating habits
Decreased saliva and gastric juice secretion may also affect nutrition

slides.title: Enteral tube feeding
text: How do we check correct  placement when a tube is first placed and with every use?

slides.title: Personal Hygiene
text: Self-care by which people attend to such functions as bathing, toileting, general body hygiene, and grooming

slides.title: Personal HygieneBathing
text: Tub bath; 43 – 46 deg C. (100 – 120 deg F.)
ROM prevents loss of muscle tone, increases circulation
Intact healthy skin 1st line of defense
Moisture can result in increased bacterial growth & irritation
Body odors caused by resident bacteria

slides.title: Provide smooth, wrinkle-free bed foundation
text: To ensure continued safety of client after making an occupied bed:
Put items used by client within easy reach

slides.title: Postmortem
text: Review organ donation if it applies
Body kept in normal anatomical position
Label the body (identification tags on bag and ankle)
Send all prostheses tagged with the body
Is there ever a circumstance when we would leave any tubes in the body?

slides.title: NGN NCLEX-RN Practice Question
text: The nurse in the outpatient clinic is talking with a 22-year-old client who is seeking treatment for constipation and given a prescription and discharge instructions for bisacodyl therapy. Which of the following statements by the client would require follow-up? Select all that apply.
“I should drink 2 to 4 glasses of water per day.”
“I will take the medication on an empty stomach to obtain quick relief from constipation.”
“I will notify my health care provider if I should experience abdominal pain without any relief.”
“I should make sure that I do not take the medication with an antacid even to prevent gastric upset.”
“I should plan on taking the medication for the rest of my life to prevent any future episodes of discomfort.”
